title: Restoring Hope in a Hopeless Generation
excerpt: A Sunday Service message from Romans 4:13–20 on Abraham’s faith: God speaks into impossible situations, hope rests on His promises, and hope in God refuses to give up.
content:
“Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed…” — Romans 4:18

Restoring Hope in a Hopeless Generation

The message called a generation surrounded by discouragement, uncertainty and seemingly impossible circumstances back to biblical hope. Its central picture was Abraham in Romans 4:13–20: a man who received a promise from God and continued believing even when the visible facts appeared to contradict what God had spoken.

“Hope is the confidence that tomorrow can be better than today.”

The sermon did not present hope as wishful thinking. Christian hope is anchored in God: in His character, His promises and His ability to accomplish what He has spoken.

Abraham: Against All Hope, He Believed

Romans 4 explains that the promise to Abraham and his offspring came through the righteousness that is by faith. Abraham therefore becomes a model for a generation learning how to trust God when circumstances look impossible.

Romans 4:18 says that against all hope, Abraham in hope believed. His circumstances did not look promising, yet he refused to make circumstances greater than God's promise.

1. God Speaks in the Impossible

God's call to Abraham was not based on what Abraham could accomplish through human strength. The Abrahamic story in Genesis 12 and Genesis 15 shows God calling, promising and leading before Abraham could see the fulfilment.

This is the first foundation of restored hope: an impossible situation does not prevent God from speaking. What appears finished to human eyes may still be the place where faith begins.

2. Hope Is Built on God's Promises

Hope must have an anchor. For Abraham, that anchor was not public opinion, age, natural ability or favourable circumstances. It was the promise of God.

The Christian journey is a marathon rather than a sprint. There are moments when progress seems slow, relationships need restoration, and circumstances tempt us to turn back. Yet the believer continues toward what God has called them to become. Philippians 3:12–14 reinforces this posture: refusing to remain imprisoned by what is behind and pressing toward the goal ahead.

3. Hope in God Refuses to Give Up

Romans 4:19–20 gives the third major lesson. Abraham did not pretend the facts were different. Scripture says he faced the reality of his own body and Sarah's womb. Biblical hope therefore does not require denying reality; it refuses to allow the facts to displace faith in God's promise.

“Without weakening in his faith…”
“Yet he did not waver through unbelief regarding the promise of God.”

The exhortation was direct: refuse to give up.

Stand Up for Jesus

At this point the message moved into the historic hymn Stand Up, Stand Up for Jesus, reinforcing the sermon’s emphasis on perseverance and spiritual courage.

Read the hymn and its history →

The message then drew on Isaiah 54:17. The prayer was not that believers would never encounter resistance, but that resistance would not stop them from becoming what God has ordained them to become.

Do Not Entertain Unbelief

The closing exhortation returned to Romans 4:20. Abraham did not waver through unbelief concerning God's promise.

“As far as God has said it, O God, I will trust You. I will believe You.”
“Challenges will not change my mind concerning how I see God. Circumstances will not change my love for God.”
“You are not what people say about you; you are what God says about you.”

Your Expectation Will Not Be Cut Off

The prayer over the younger generation was that God would restore hope and that their expectation would not be cut off, echoing Proverbs 23:18. Students were invited to place their studies, careers, future and destiny before God and refuse hopelessness.

Leave the Ninety-Nine and Go for the One

The final movement turned restored hope outward. The church was challenged not to keep hope to itself, but to seek students who have drifted away or feel spiritually lost.

“We must leave the ninety-nine and go for one.”

The congregation was urged to call that brother, that sister, that student—to intentionally reach people rather than waiting for them to return on their own. This reflects Jesus' picture of seeking the one who is lost in Luke 15:3–7 and Matthew 18:12–14.

A Final Declaration of Hope

The service closed in corporate prayer against hopelessness, pessimism, discouragement and the temptation to give up.

“I declare my victory. I shall make it in my career. My destiny is secure. My future is secure.”

God speaks in the impossible. Hope is built on God's promises. Hope in God refuses to give up.

Scriptures from the Message

  • Romans 4:13–20
  • Genesis 12; 15
  • Philippians 3:12–14
  • Isaiah 54:17
  • Proverbs 23:18
  • Luke 15:3–7; Matthew 18:12–14
